saffire-vi-3: A two-sided PMMA material measuring 1 cm thick and 18 cm, with an oxygen percentage of 30.3, a pressure of 7.9 psi, and an airflow of 20 cm/s concurrent, cut to 5 cm/s at 1120 s, was tested in the Saffire-VI investigation. The material burned for 780 s, resulting in an O2-calorimetry total of 1280 kJ with a peak of 3080 W, a max temperature of 77 C at the SFU outlet and 21 C at the FFD, a CO2 rise of 8539 ppm, and a CO rise of 308 ppm.
saffire-vi-4: One-sided PMMA, 0.5 cm thick, 18 cm was tested at an oxygen level of 28.8%, a pressure of 8.0 psi, and an airflow of 20 cm/s concurrent. The material burned for 1200 s, producing an O2-calorimetry total of 830 kJ with a peak of 1507 W, a maximum temperature of 57 C at SFU outlet and 21 C at FFD, a CO2 rise of 8117 ppm, and a CO rise of 320 ppm.
saffire-v-2: A cotton jersey measuring 50 cm was tested in an environment with an oxygen percentage of 26.2, a pressure of 10.3 psi, and an airflow of 20 cm/s concurrent. The material burned for 200 s, resulting in a total fuel-calorimetry heat release of 560 kJ, a maximum temperature of 46 C at SFU outlet and 23 C at FFD, a CO2 rise of 2360 ppm, and a CO rise of 83 ppm.
